scenario: Discussing weekend plans with a friend
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Igbo

vocabulary.note: common verb for movement, often used with destinations
relative pronoun or determiner, very common in Igbo
can also mean 'time' in some contexts

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Emeela gị zụ n'ime ubochi nke à? Gị nke ka m agụ? Kedu nụ?
dialogue.translation: Have you made plans for this weekend? Which one should I do? What about you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: M nụ̀, m ga-ezụ ọnụ n'ime ubochi nke à. Ọ bụrụ na ọnụ gị kà dị, ị ga-ezụ ụzọ nụ̀?
dialogue.translation: And I will just relax this weekend. If you have time, will you come too?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: À, m ga-ezụ ọ bụla nke m chọrọ. Ọ bụ nke àgụ n'ụlọ ndụ nụ̀?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I will do whatever I want. Or is it work at the hospital?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ọ dịghị. M ga-agụ ọnụ n'ime ulo akwụkwọ nke ụlọ ndụ mbido.
dialogue.translation: No. I will relax inside the new school library.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ọ bụrụ na ọnụ gị dị, ị ga-ezụ ndị nwere ike n'ime ubochi nke à.
dialogue.translation: If you have time, you can invite those who are free this weekend.

key_phrases.translation: Have you made plans for this weekend?

key_phrases.translation: I will just relax this weekend.

key_phrases.translation: Is it work?

key_phrases.phrase: Ọ dịghị. M ga-agụ ọnụ.
key_phrases.translation: No. I will relax.

key_phrases.phrase: Ọ bụrụ na ọnụ gị dị, ị ga-ezụ ndị nwere ike.
key_phrases.translation: If you have time, you can invite those who are free.

scenario: Describing symptoms at a pharmacy

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Biko, m chọrọ ịgụ ugwu. E nwere m ọkụ.
dialogue.translation: Please, I need to take medicine. I have a fever.

dialogue.speaker: Pharmacist
dialogue.text: Ụtụtụ ị bụ ebe ị tụrụ ụkwụ?
dialogue.translation: Where does your foot hurt?

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Ụtụtụ ụkwụ m dị n'ebe tinyere ugwu elu. E nwere m nri ịchọrọ.

dialogue.text: Kedu ugwu ị nwere? Biko zụta ugwu ndoro ọ bụ ugwu elu?

scenario: Talking about your hometown to a visitor
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Igbo

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ụlọ ahịa dị n'okpuru ebe m na-adị. M kpatara ị banye?
dialogue.translation: The market is under the place where I live. Can I explain how to go there?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ee, biko kpatara m! M nwere ike ịmụ nni ndị a ga-eji na-egosi ebe ahịa.
dialogue.translation: Yes, please explain it to me! I would like to know the food they usually use to show the market.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ọ bụ mgbidi n'ime nkwu. M ga-eme ka ị gba oge n'ụlọ mmiri n'okpuru.
dialogue.translation: It's the bridge in the story. I will let you play a game under the water house.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Kedu ka ndị ebe ahịa nwere nni ndị a? Anyị ga-emeri nni n'ebe ahịa?
dialogue.translation: How do the people at the market have this food? Will we eat the food at the market?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ee, tụpu anyị ga-emeri nni, anyị ga-egosi nkwu ndị ọma. Ọ bụrụ na ị chọrọ, anyị ga-eme ka ị gba.
dialogue.translation: Yes, before we eat the food, we will tell good stories. If you want, we will let you play.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Dị mma. M ga-eme ka m ịmụ nkwu ndị a tụpu anyị ga-emeri nni!
dialogue.translation: Good. I will make sure I know these stories before we eat the food!

key_phrases.phrase: M kpatara ị banye?
key_phrases.translation: Can I explain how to go there?

key_phrases.phrase: Ọ bụ mgbidi n'ime nkwu.
key_phrases.translation: It's the bridge in the story.

key_phrases.phrase: Kedu ka ndị ebe ahịa nwere nni ndị a?
key_phrases.translation: How do the people at the market have this food?

key_phrases.phrase: Anyị ga-eme ka ị gba.
key_phrases.translation: We will let you play.

dialogue.text: Kedu aha gị? Nke ukwuu ị ga-eme nni ahụ tupu anyị tinye ọnwanyi ị nkwu.
dialogue.translation: What is your name? We’ll do this before we confirm your new room assignment.

dialogue.speaker: Guest

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist

dialogue.translation: There are some new rooms in that hotel. For this change, you’ll get a new room.

dialogue.text: Daalụ! Ọ dị mma ịnụ ọnwanyi ndoro nke agụ.
dialogue.translation: Thank you! I’m happy to get this new room.

scenario: Planning a birthday party
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Igbo

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Biko, gị ka ị kpọ ndoro n'ime ngwa a si chịọ. Nkàdọ m nkwado gị ma kà ị nwere ohu siri ike.
dialogue.translation: Please, you should call me about the money mentioned in this thing. I will help you and you will have enough strength.

dialogue.speaker: Obi
dialogue.text: Ezi, m ga-esi! Ma ọnwụ ụlọ ndoro ahu dịla, n'ihi na ndoro zuzu ka ị nwere ike ịtọ ike.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I will say! But that house money is too much, because money is scarce and you need strength.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Nke ahu dịla ka ị nwere ike ịtọ ike dị ka ndoro zuzu. Ma m ga-ewere nkwado gị, ọ dị mma.
dialogue.translation: That one is such that you can be strong as money is scarce. But I will take your help, it is good.

dialogue.speaker: Obi
dialogue.text: Kedu n'ime ngwa ahu, ndoro zuzu ahu dị mma ka m gị nkwado?
dialogue.translation: What about this thing, is the scarce money good for me to help you?

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Ee, ndoro zuzu ahu dị mma ka ị gị nkwado n'ọma. Ya mere, ị ga-esi ka m kpọ gị n'ime ụlọ.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the scarce money is good for you to help me properly. Because of that, you should tell me when you come to the house.
